title: Who decides the next step: fixed sequences and model-driven loops

items.stem: A pharmacy script sends each scanned prescription to a language model, which replies with one label: refill, interaction-check or other. The script has a separate block of code for each label, and each block runs its own steps in a set order. A teammate says the model is steering the system, so it is a model-driven loop. What is the accurate response?

options.text: Agreed, because any model output that selects a branch hands over the flow
Disagreed, because the model only supplies a label and the code fixes what follows
Agreed, because several model calls in one run each shape what happens later
Disagreed, because a loop needs the model to call a tool, and none is called

items.stem: A router company builds a helper for customers who write "my wifi drops every evening". Possible checks are reading router logs, testing signal strength, comparing firmware versions and scanning for channel congestion. Across 200 past support cases, between one and six checks were run, in 41 different orders, and the first result often redirected the rest. Which design fits?

options.text: Run all four checks in one fixed order for everyone, then write up the results
Make one model call that reads the complaint and writes a diagnosis directly
Have a model pick one scripted check sequence once, before any check runs
Let a model choose each next check from the results so far, until it can diagnose

items.stem: A lab processes 300 incident forms a night. A fixed prototype makes 3 model calls per form. A loop prototype, where the model chooses each next action, averages 7 calls per form, and across 300 traces the actions it chose were identical in every one. In one sentence, what does the extra spending buy?

Your team must add a feature that summarizes lab incident reports. Nobody yet knows how much the reports vary or what a good summary needs, and the model budget is small. Which starting point best limits cost and risk?

options.text: Build a model-driven loop with many tools, so it can adapt to varied reports
Build one fixed sequence of steps and keep it, since it is the cheapest option
Build a fixed sequence, measure where it fails, and add flexibility only there
Build several cooperating model-driven loops, one specialist per report type

items.stem: A bank's refund assistant is a loop in which the model picks from verify_identity, look_up_order and issue_refund. The bank requires identity verification before every refund, without exception. In 2 of 200 test runs the model called issue_refund first, although its prompt says to verify first. Which change addresses the cause?

options.text: Have the code run the identity check before the model is given any other tool
Move the rule into the system prompt and add an example of the correct order
Switch to a larger model, which should follow the written rule more reliably
Add a tool that tells the model whether the identity has already been verified

items.stem: A makerspace assistant is one loop where the model chooses among search_manuals, check_calendar and book_machine, capped at 8 steps. A menu button already tells the system whether a request is a booking. In all 80 booking traces the tool calls were identical, while the manual questions took very different routes. To cut cost and make bookings reliable, what is the best change?

options.text: Raise the cap from 8 to 15 steps so long manual questions are not cut off
Run bookings as fixed steps in code, and keep the loop for manual questions
Add worked booking examples to the prompt so the loop gets the order right
Give manuals and bookings each their own loop, with their own tools
